column3: Begin single-line source comment on current line
column10: Begins a comment that, when represented in EM (Ember Language source) format, should be displayed as a “#”-style comment. All characters except 248 and 255 will be ignored. Use 255 248 to represent 248 within the comment, and 255 255 to represent 255 within the comment.

column3: Begin single-line source comment on new line
column10: As with 247, but starting on a new line in the source form.
Terminates a comment region begun by 246 or 247.

column3: Begin block source comment on current line
column10: As with 248, but creating a “/*  */”-style block comment.

column3: Begin block source comment on new line
column10: As with 250, but starting on a new line in the source form.
Terminates a comment region begun by 249 or 250.
Indicates that a line break that would normally be present at this point in source form should be instead represented by a ;.
Indicates that the current logical line should be split into two physical lines in source form, joined using \.
Indicates that the following logical block of statements should be bundled onto a single line of the source, joined using ; and bundled using { and }.
Send the specified string to the current output context, adding a final line feed if one is not present
Frames one value expression as a parameter. A literal parameter remains quoted data.
Terminates the parameter begun by 258 after its complete value expression.

Begins a typed quoted character sequence. The payload may be empty. Dc 255 protects exactly the next Dc from syntactic interpretation: 255 261 is payload Dc 261 and 255 255 is payload Dc 255. Only an unescaped 261 terminates the literal. Decode escapes once after locating the boundary; payload characters are not implicitly evaluated or reparsed.
Terminates a literal begun by 260 unless protected by Dc 255 within its payload.
A specific case of “String” as a format (short-style format ID 80)
Invoke the routine with the given name
Indicates a division between blocks of statements
Indicates that in source form, there is FIXME: following amount of whitespace., a blank line should be present here

Begins a nonempty name. Dc 255 protects exactly the following Dc from syntactic interpretation. Only an unescaped 271 terminates the name. The name is data; reference or invocation syntax determines how it is used.
Terminates an identifier begun by 270 unless protected by Dc 255 within its payload.
Indicates the point at which an indented block is left and execution returns to the enclosing block

column10: References the named object with an optional explicit type. Both forms begin with 276 and end with the complete framed identifier. Resolve the reference only in an evaluation context; quoting it does not perform a lookup.

Subtype of string
Begins an ordered, contiguous, typed homogenous or heterogenous list.
Terminates a typed list begun by 310. Optionally, a length can be specified, in which case it must have that many elements declared.
Separates elements within a list or sequence.

Legacy ordered key-value associative map. Keys and values alternate with Dc 312 between every operand. The optional length counts pairs. Retained for reading existing documents; new documents should use Dc 559.
Terminates a legacy ordered key-value associative map begun by 313.
Indicates an optional value is present.
Indicates an optional value is absent.

Begins a key-value pair. Dc 312 separates the nonempty key and value regions; Dc 515 closes the pair. Nested framed data and escaped characters belong to their operand rather than delimiting the enclosing pair. Operand regions retain their historical syntax; this rule does not impose a narrower expression grammar.
Terminates the key-value pair begun by Dc 514.

References a value declared by Dc 269 in the current or nearest enclosing identifier scope. The identifier is name data; evaluating the reference resolves its value. Quoting the reference does not perform lookup.

Enters a lexical identifier scope. Inner Dc 269 declarations shadow outer declarations of the same name and may produce warnings. Declarations last only until scope exit and never cross document boundaries by default.
Exits the innermost identifier scope and discards its declarations. Outer declarations become visible again. All document-local declarations expire at the end of the document.

Begins an ordered key-value associative map of adjacent explicitly closed Dc 514 pairs. No Dc 312 occurs between pairs. The optional length counts pairs. The declared key and value types apply to each pair; inherited declarations must accompany independently extracted fragments. Invalid pair framing must not be reinterpreted as the legacy Dc 313 form.
Terminates an ordered key-value associative map begun by Dc 559.

column3: Built-in type identifier: Atom Dc (unevaluated Document Character reference)
column10: An unevaluated reference to a single Document Character (or Dc 616 atom expression), denoting the character or graph node itself rather than evaluating its syntax rule.
Evaluates or asserts the first operand ([statement]) once for each element of the second operand, binding Dc 639 (This element) to the current element on each iteration.

Pronoun referring to the element currently being iterated over within an enclosing Dc 638 (Distribute statement over each element) expression. (The Dc is called "This" by analogy to jQuery $(this) in .each(), but maybe there's a better name for it.)
Begins a tokenized module containing an optional namespace declaration, zero or more use imports, and zero or more top-level items.
Terminates a module begun by Dc 2192.
Declares the PSR-4 module namespace path of the enclosing module.
Imports one or more exported bindings or routines from the specified namespace path.
Terminates a use import list begun by Dc 2195.
Specifies one imported item (by resolved Dc or source identifier) and an optional local alias identifier.
Declares a non-shadowing local mutable variable of the given type, with an optional initial value expression.
Declares a private immutable binding with an optional assigned graph Dc identity, static type, name, and initializer expression.
Declares an exported module-level immutable binding with an optional assigned graph Dc identity, static type, name, and initializer expression.
Assigns a new value expression to an existing mutable local variable of matching type.
References a lexically bound variable or constant (by identifier or resolved graph Dc) with its explicit static type.

Declares a named routine with a boolean export visibility flag (true for public, false for private), optional assigned graph Dc identity, return type, name, typed parameters, optional test block, and body expression.
Terminates a routine declaration begun by Dc 2203.
Declares one formal parameter of a routine with its static type and identifier.
Begins a contract block of one or more inline input/output test cases attached to a routine declaration.
Terminates a routine test block begun by Dc 2206.
Defines one inline routine test case consisting of positional argument expressions, Dc 2209, and the expected output expression (or FaultTrap for expected traps, or absent for void completion).
Separates positional input argument expressions from the expected output within a Dc 2208 test case.
Terminates a routine test case begun by Dc 2208.
Invokes a local or resolved graph routine with zero or more positional argument expressions.
Terminates a routine call begun by Dc 2211.
Evaluates zero or more sequential expressions or local declarations in a new lexical scope, yielding the final expression's value (or void if empty).
Terminates a code block begun by Dc 2213.
Evaluates a boolean condition expression and branches to either the second operand (then) or third operand (else).
Repeatedly evaluates the boolean condition expression and executes the void body expression while true.
Iterates over a sequence expression in order, binding a fresh non-shadowing element identifier of the declared type for each iteration of the body expression.
Exits the innermost enclosing loop immediately (type Never).
Advances immediately to the next iteration of the innermost enclosing loop (type Never).
Returns early from the enclosing routine with an optional return value expression (or absent for void routines; type Never).
Deterministically aborts execution with an unrecoverable trap (type Never).
Checked numeric addition of two operands of matching type; faults on overflow.
Checked subtraction of the second operand from the first operand; faults on overflow.
Checked numeric multiplication of two operands of matching type; faults on overflow.
Checked truncated division of the first operand by the second operand; faults on division by zero or signed minimum divided by -1.
Checked truncated remainder of dividing the first operand by the second operand; faults on zero divisor or signed minimum modulo -1.
Checked arithmetic negation of a signed operand; faults on two's-complement minimum value.
Modular two's-complement addition wrapping modulo 2^width on fixed-width integers.
Modular two's-complement subtraction of the second operand from the first operand wrapping modulo 2^width.
Modular two's-complement multiplication wrapping modulo 2^width on fixed-width integers.
Bitwise conjunction of two integer operands of matching type.
Bitwise inclusive disjunction of two integer operands of matching type.
Bitwise exclusive disjunction of two integer operands of matching type.
Bitwise ones'-complement inversion of an integer operand.
Shifts the first integer operand left by the second u32 bit-count operand; faults if the shift count is greater than or equal to the bit width.

Shifts the first integer operand right by the second u32 bit-count operand (logical zero-fill on unsigned types, arithmetic sign-extending on signed types); faults if the shift count is greater than or equal to the bit width.
Bitwise left rotation of the first unsigned integer operand by the second u32 bit-count operand.
Bitwise right rotation of the first unsigned integer operand by the second u32 bit-count operand.
Counts leading zero bits in a fixed-width integer operand as a u32.
Counts trailing zero bits in a fixed-width integer operand as a u32.
Counts set one-bits in a fixed-width integer operand as a u32.
Boolean negation of a boolean operand.
Short-circuiting boolean conjunction: evaluates the second operand only when the first operand is true.
Short-circuiting boolean disjunction: evaluates the second operand only when the first operand is false.
Tests whether two operands of matching type are equal (including structural element-wise equality on immutable lists).
Tests whether two operands of matching type are not equal.
Tests whether the first operand is strictly less than the second operand.
Tests whether the first operand is less than or equal to the second operand.
Tests whether the first operand is strictly greater than the second operand.
Tests whether the first operand is greater than or equal to the second operand.
Converts the first operand's numeric value to the target type specified by the second operand (lossless when widening, faulting when outside the target type's range).
Reinterprets the raw bit pattern of the first fixed-width integer operand as a same-width integer of the target type specified by the second operand.
Returns the element count of a sequence or buffer as a u64.
Reads the element of the first sequence/buffer operand at the zero-based u64 index given by the second operand; faults when out of bounds.
Extracts the half-open sub-sequence [start..end) from the first operand using the second (start) and third (end) u64 index operands; faults unless start <= end <= length.
Returns a new immutable sequence containing all elements of the first operand followed by all elements of the second operand.
Parameterized immutable value-semantics StageL list type l/T over element type T.
Parameterized mutable local StageL buffer type buf/T over element type T for linear-time construction and O(1) indexed updates.
Constructs an immutable StageL list of the specified element type from zero or more evaluated element expressions.
Terminates a StageL list constructor begun by Dc 2578.
Allocates an empty mutable StageL buffer of the specified element type with initial u64 capacity given by the second operand.
Allocates a mutable StageL buffer initialized with copies of the first element-value operand repeated to the u64 length given by the second operand.
Appends the second element operand to the end of the first mutable StageL buffer operand in amortized O(1) time; faults if the buffer has been frozen.
Appends all elements of the second immutable list operand to the end of the first mutable StageL buffer operand; faults if the buffer has been frozen.
Overwrites the element of the first mutable StageL buffer operand at the zero-based u64 index (second operand) with the third operand in O(1) time; faults if out of bounds or frozen.
Freezes a mutable StageL buffer into an immutable l/T list in O(1) zero-copy time and marks the buffer handle frozen against subsequent mutation.
